q: Which feature is found in ALL cervical vertebrae and in no other vertebrae?
options: A foramen transversarium (hole in the transverse process)
why: Every cervical vertebra has a foramen transversarium. The vertebral artery runs through it from C6 up to C1. Bifid spines are only typical of C3–C6, and rib facets belong to thoracic vertebrae.

q: Which vertebra has no body and no spinous process?
why: The atlas is a ring of an anterior arch, a posterior arch and two lateral masses. Its 'body' became the dens of the axis.

q: Shaking your head to say "no" happens mainly at which joint?
why: The atlas turns around the dens of the axis at the atlanto-axial joint ('no'). Nodding 'yes' happens at the atlanto-occipital joint between the skull and C1.

q: Which ligament holds the dens against the back of the anterior arch of the atlas?
why: The transverse ligament runs behind the dens like a belt. If it tears, the dens can press on the spinal cord.

q: Which cervical vertebra can you easily feel at the back of the neck when you bend your head forward?
why: C7 is the vertebra prominens: its long, non-bifid spinous process is the first bump you feel at the base of the neck.
